'''Hitaka Shrine''' (日高神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Mizusawa|en|Mizusawa|qid=Q1114302|lt=Mizusawa, Ōshū, Iwate}}, {{ill|Ōshū, Iwate|en|Ōshū, Iwate|qid=Q386052|lt=Ōshū, Iwate}}, {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}}. It was classified as a former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}}.

The shrine is known for its {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}-designated main hall and the {{ill|Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja|日高火防祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日高火防祭り|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11510844}}.

== Name ==

[[File:日高神社参道.JPG|thumb|right|200px|The sacred forest and the approach to Hitaka Shrine]]

The origin of the shrine's name has multiple theories. One suggests that the area was historically known as {{ill|Hitakami|en|Hitakami|qid=Q11288931|lt=Hitakami no Kuni}} and served as a central location for its people. Another tradition states that during the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Former Nine Years' War}}, {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} prayed at this shrine, and soon after, the rain ceased, the sun rose high in the sky, and by the Hour of the Goat (around 2 PM), he successfully defeated {{ill|Abe no Sadato|en|Abe no Sadato|qid=Q3616500|lt=Abe no Sadatō}}.

The shrine is also referred to as "Hitaka Myōken" or "Hitaka Myōken-gū" due to its association with {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken}}, a Buddhist deity.

== Deities ==

The shrine enshrines the following eight deities:
* {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}
* {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|ja|火産霊神|lt=Kagutsuchi}}
* {{ill|Toshigami|fr|Toshigami|it|Toshigami|ja|年神|mni|ꯇꯣꯁꯤꯒꯃꯤ|pl|Toshigami|ru|Тосигами|simple|Toshigami|uk|Тосіґамі|zh|年神|qid=Q3028663|lt=Ōtoshi-no-kami}}
* {{ill|Toshigami|fr|Toshigami|it|Toshigami|ja|年神|mni|ꯇꯣꯁꯤꯒꯃꯤ|pl|Toshigami|ru|Тосигами|simple|Toshigami|uk|Тосіґамі|zh|年神|qid=Q3028663}}
* Wakatoshi-no-Kami
* {{ill|Mizuhanome|it|Mizuhanome|ja|ミヅハノメ|pl|Mizuhanome|sv|Mizuhanome|zh|彌都波能賣神|qid=Q8191796|lt=Mizuha-no-Me}}
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama}}

Ame-no-Minakanushi is frequently syncretized with {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken}}.

== History ==

=== Founding Legend ===

According to tradition, Hitaka Shrine was established in the 1st year of the {{ill|Kōnin (era)|en|Kōnin (era)|qid=Q1373070|lt=Kōnin era}} (810) by imperial decree of {{ill|Emperor Saga|ar|الإمبراطور ساغا|azb|ساقا (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Сага|bn|সম্রাট সাগা|ca|Saga Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر ساگا|cs|Saga|de|Saga (Tennō)|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σάγκα|eo|Saga (imperiestro)|es|Saga Tennō|eu|Saga enperadorea|fa|امپراتور ساگا|fr|Saga (empereur)|id|Kaisar Saga|it|Saga (imperatore del Giappone)|ja|嵯峨天皇|ko|사가 천황|nl|Saga (keizer)|pl|Saga (cesarz)|pt|Saga (imperador)|ru|Император Сага|sh|Car Saga|simple|Emperor Saga|sl|Cesar Saga|sv|Saga (kejsare)|sw|Saga wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิซางะ|tl|Emperador Saga|tr|Saga (imparator)|uk|Імператор Саґа|vi|Thiên hoàng Saga|yo|Emperor Saga|zh|嵯峨天皇|zh_min_nan|Saga Thian-hông|qid=Q316654|lt=Emperor Saga}}. This event occurred eight years after the submission of {{ill|Aterui|cs|Aterui|fa|آته‌روی|ja|アテルイ|ko|아테루이|no|Aterui|pt|Aterui|zh|阿弖流為|qid=Q1088046|lt=Aterui}} and the construction of {{ill|Isawa Castle|fa|قلعه ایساوا|ja|胆沢城|qid=Q11611683|lt=Fort Isawa}} by {{ill|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|bn|সাকানোউয়ে নো তামারামারো|ca|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|de|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|el|Σακανόουε νο Ταμουραμάρο|es|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|eu|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|fa|ساکانواوئه نو تامورامارو|fr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|it|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ja|坂上田村麻呂|ko|사카노우에노 다무라마로|pl|Tamuramaro Sakanoue|pt|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|ru|Саканоуэ-но Тамурамаро|simple|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|sl|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|tr|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|uk|Саканоуе но Тамурамаро|vi|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|zh|坂上田村麻呂|zh_classical|坂上田村麻呂|zh_min_nan|Sakanoue no Tamuramaro|qid=Q941979|lt=Sakanoue no Tamuramaro}} in 802. It is believed that the shrine was created as part of the central government's efforts to integrate local beliefs with those of the Yamato court.

=== Heian Period and Beyond ===

The shrine was visited for battle prayers by {{ill|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|en|Minamoto no Yoriyoshi|qid=Q3082851|lt=Minamoto no Yoriyoshi}} and his son {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|cs|Jošiie Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoshiie|es|Minamoto no Yoshiie|eu|Minamoto no Yoshiie|fa|میناموتو نو یوشی‌ایه|fr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|it|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家|ko|미나모토노 요시이에|pt|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ro|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ru|Минамото-но Ёсииэ|sh|Minamoto no Yoshiie|sv|Minamoto no Yoshiie|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยชิอิเอะ|tr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|uk|Мінамото но Йосіїе|zh|源義家|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} during both the {{ill|Former Nine Years' War|en|Former Nine Years' War|qid=Q1187448|lt=Former Nine Years' War}} and the {{ill|Gosannen War|cs|Pozdní tříletá válka|es|Guerra Gosannen|fa|جنگ گوساننن|fr|Guerre de Gosannen|ja|後三年の役|ka|გოსანნენის ომი|ko|후3년의 역|pt|Guerra Gosannen|ru|Война Госаннэн|th|สงครามโกะซันเน็ง|uk|Трирічна війна|zh|後三年之役|qid=Q1187411|lt=Later Three Years' War}}. It was also revered by the {{ill|Rusu clan|ja|伊沢氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izawa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 留守氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2975345}}, the {{ill|Northern Fujiwara|en|Northern Fujiwara|qid=Q1050942|lt=Northern Fujiwara}}, and later by the {{ill|Date clan|en|Date clan|qid=Q1151061|lt=Date clan}}.

In 1170 (2nd year of {{ill|Kaō (era)|en|Kaō (era)|qid=Q1150842|lt=Kaō era}}), {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidehira|en|Fujiwara no Hidehira|qid=Q3090625|lt=Fujiwara no Hidehira}} sponsored the reconstruction of the shrine.<ref>‘''Rikuchū Province Isawa District Village Records''’ (陸中国胆沢郡村誌, 1880). Notably, this was the same year Hidehira was appointed Chinjufu-shōgun (鎮守府将軍).</ref> During the late 16th century, {{ill|Date Masamune|en|Date Masamune|qid=Q311183|lt=Date Masamune}} contributed to its rebuilding and granted shrine lands. In 1632 (9th year of {{ill|Kan'ei|en|Kan'ei|qid=Q1192913|lt=Kan'ei era}}), {{ill|Date Munetosi|ja|留守宗利|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lusumune Tadayoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11237935}}, the first lord of {{ill|Mizusawa Castle|ja|水沢城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizusawa Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11548846}}, ordered the reconstruction of the main shrine building.

=== Modern Era ===

In 1869 (2nd year of {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}), Hitaka Shrine became the general shrine of {{ill|Isawa Prefecture|ja|胆沢県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isawa Prefecture|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11611687}}. In 1874, it was designated as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} (a significant local shrine). This Ranking system was abolished in 1946.

== Shrine Buildings ==

The main shrine building, constructed in 1632, features a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a copper roof. It was designated an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} in 1990 for its unique Edo-period architectural features.<ref>[http://www.bunka.pref.iwate.jp/ciss/bunkazai/detail/id/33 Iwate Prefecture Cultural Heritage Database - Hitaka Shrine Main Hall]</ref>

'''Hitaka Shrine''' (日高神社, ひたかじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Mizusawa, Iwate|en|Mizusawa, Iwate|qid=Q1133151|lt=Mizusawa, Ōshū}}, {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}}. The shrine is known for its **Important Cultural Property-designated main hall** and the **Hitaka Hibuse Festival** (日高火防祭).

== Name ==
[[File:日高神社参道.JPG|thumb|right|200px|Hitaka Shrine's sacred forest and the approach along Hitaka Kōji]]
There are multiple theories regarding the origin of the shrine's name. Some suggest that the region was historically called **Hitakami Province (日高見国)** and served as the center of power for the **Hitakami forces**. Another tradition attributes the name to **Minamoto no Yoshiie**'s prayer during the **Former Nine Years' War (前九年の役)**, when after his supplication, the rain **su11enly stopped, and the sun rose high in the sky** at the hour of the goat (**around 2 PM**), allowing him to **defeat Abe no Sadatō**.

Since the shrine also enshrines **Myōken Bosatsu**, it has been referred to as **Hitaka Myōken** or **Hitaka Myōken-gū**.

- {{ill|Mizuhanome|it|Mizuhanome|ja|ミヅハノメ|pl|Mizuhanome|sv|Mizuhanome|zh|彌都波能賣神|qid=Q8191796}}

Ame-no-Minakanushi is **often syncretized** with **Myōken Bosatsu**.

== History ==

=== Foundation ===
According to tradition, **Hitaka Shrine** was founded in **Kōnin 1 (810)** under an **imperial edict** from **Emperor Saga**. This occurred **eight years** after the **surrender of Aterui**, the local chief, and the establishment of **Fort Taga (胆沢城)** in **Enryaku 21 (802)** by **Sakanoue no Tamuramaro**. The shrine was likely built as part of an effort to **integrate local religious traditions** with the **central government's deities**, making it the **guardian shrine of the Taga Chinjufu (胆沢鎮守府, the regional military government)**.

=== Development in the Heian Period and Beyond ===
During the **Former Nine Years' War (前九年の役)** and **Later Three Years' War (後三年の役)**, **Minamoto no Yoriyoshi** and **Minamoto no Yoshiie** prayed at the shrine for victory. The shrine was also venerated by **Tohoku governors**, including the **Izawa clan** (later known as the **Rusu clan**), the **Ōshū Fujiwara clan**, and the **Date clan**.

In **Kaō 2 (1170)**, **Fujiwara no Hidehira** rebuilt the shrine.<ref>*Rikuchū-koku Isawa-gun Sonshi* (陸中国胆沢郡村誌, 1880). This was also the year Hidehira was appointed **Chinjufu Shōgun (鎮守府将軍)**.</ref>  
During the **Keichō era** (late 16th century), **Date Masamune** restored the shrine, donating land and constructing new buildings. Records indicate he **personally visited the shrine**.  
In **Kan'ei 9 (1632)**, the **first lord of Mizusawa Castle, Rusu Munetoshi** (伊達宗利) renovated the current main shrine building.

=== Modern Era ===
When **Isawa Prefecture** (胆沢県) was established in **Meiji 2 (1869)**, Hitaka Shrine was designated the **sōsha (総社, regional shrine)** and officially Ranked as a **gōsha** in **Meiji 4 (1871)**. However, the **gōsha Ranking system** was abolished in **Shōwa 21 (1946)**.

== Festivals ==

- **Spring Festival** – **April 22**  
- **Summer Festival** – **August 22**  

The **spring festival** was traditionally held on **Lunar New Year’s Day (旧暦正月22日)** and was accompanied by the **Hibuse Festival (火防祭, "Fire Prevention Festival")**, which is now held on the **last Saturday of April**.

The **Hibuse Festival** originated when **Rusu Munekage**, lord of Mizusawa Castle, experienced the **Great Meireki Fire** in Edo. Upon returning, he **organized a fire brigade** and offered prayers to **Hitaka Shrine ("Hi" = Fire) and Mizuyama Shrine ("Mizu" = Water)**. The festival features **Hibuse Bayashi (fire prevention music), a form of traditional music designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Iwate Prefecture**, performed as **festival floats parade through the town**. (See: {{ill|Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja|日高火防祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hitaka Hibuse Festival|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日高火防祭り|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11510844}})

== Shrine Buildings ==
[[File:日高神社拝殿.JPG|thumb|right|200px|Hitaka Shrine Worship Hall]]
- **Main Hall** (本殿): San'gensha Nagare-zukuri, copper roof (formerly thatched).  
- Rebuilt by **Rusu Munetoshi** in **Kan'ei 9 (1632)**.  
- Features **elaborate carvings**, a **unique rainbow beam (虹梁)**, and **intricate wooden joinery**, incorporating **Muromachi-period techniques**.  
- Designated a **National Important Cultural Property** in **Heisei 2 (1990)**.

- **Hibuse Bayashi (日高囃子, "Hitaka Festival Music")** (無形民俗文化財, Shōwa 38, 1963)

'''Ōshū City Cultural Properties'''
- **Stone Lanterns (6 units)** (有形文化財, Shōwa 49, 1974)
- **Rusu Clan Cemetery** (史跡, Shōwa 49, 1974)
- **Two Giant Cedars (姥杉, "Granny Cedars")** (天然記念物, Shōwa 32, 1957 / Shōwa 47, 1972)
